questions.question: A sales man offers the following scheme discount on the sale of pencils in his shop: 'Buy 20 and get 5 free'. What is the percentage of his scheme discount?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a 'Buy X Get Y Free' scheme, the discount percentage is calculated on the total number of items obtained.

Discount % = [Free Items ÷ (Paid Items + Free Items)] × 100

⇒ Discount % = [5 ÷ (20 + 5)] × 100

⇒ Discount % = (5 ÷ 25) × 100 = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Paid items = 20

Free items = 5

 Total 25 Pencils (Marked Price Basis)
 
 
 20 Paid Pencils (Selling Price)
 5 Free
 

 Discount = 5 Free Pencils out of 25 Total
 Discount % = (5 ÷ 25) × 100 = 20%

**Method Used:**

Let the Marked Price (MP) of 1 pencil be ₹1.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total items taken by the customer = 20 + 5 = 25 pencils.

⇒ Total Marked Price (MP) of 25 pencils = 25 × ₹1 = ₹25.

⇒ Since the customer pays only for 20 pencils, the Selling Price (SP) for all 25 pencils = 20 × ₹1 = ₹20.

⇒ Discount Amount = MP − SP = 25 − 20 = ₹5.

⇒ Discount Percentage = (Discount Amount ÷ MP) × 100

⇒ Discount Percentage = (5 ÷ 25) × 100 = 20%.

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Buy X Get Y Free Schemes

In these promotional offers, the base for calculating the discount percentage is always the total number of items obtained (X + Y), not just the paid items.

Successive Discounts

When two discounts d₁% and d₂% are given one after another, the effective discount is [d₁ + d₂ − (d₁ × d₂) ÷ 100]%.

Marked Price & Selling Price

The Selling Price (SP) is obtained after subtracting the discount from the Marked Price (MP). Formula: SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100.

questions.question: There are 49 members in group A, 35 members in group B and 31 members in group C. All the members of these groups went to a restaurant. The average amount spent on each member of group A, B and C is ₹106, ₹141 and ₹226, respectively. The total average amount (in ₹) spent per member is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the assumed average be ₹141 (Average of Group B).

Net deviation = [49 × (106 − 141)] + [35 × (141 − 141)] + [31 × (226 − 141)]

⇒ Net deviation = 49 × (−35) + 0 + 31 × 85 = −1715 + 2635 = +920

Average deviation = +920 ÷ (49 + 35 + 31) = +920 ÷ 115 = +8

Actual average = Assumed average + Average deviation = 141 + 8 = 149

**∴ The correct answer is ₹149.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of members in Group A = 49, Average amount = ₹106

Number of members in Group B = 35, Average amount = ₹141

Number of members in Group C = 31, Average amount = ₹226

**Formula Used:**

Total Average = Total Amount ÷ Total Members

questions.question: Two trains are moving in opposite directions at speeds of 60 km/h and 50 km/h. The length of one train is 430 m. The time taken by them to cross each other is 44 seconds. The length (in m ) of the other train, correct to 2 decimal places, is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Relative speed (opposite directions) = 60 + 50 = 110 km/h = 110 × 5/18 = 275/9 m/s

Total distance covered = Relative speed × Time = (275/9) × 44 = 12100/9 ≈ 1344.44 m

Length of second train = Total distance − Length of first train

Length of second train = 1344.44 − 430 = 914.44 m

**∴ The correct answer is 914.44 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of Train 1 (S₁) = 60 km/h

Speed of Train 2 (S₂) = 50 km/h

Length of Train 1 (L₁) = 430 m

Time to cross each other = 44 seconds

**Formula Used:**

When two objects move in opposite directions, Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂

Total Distance = Speed × Time

When two trains cross each other, Total Distance = Sum of the lengths of the two trains.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Relative Speed = 60 + 50 = 110 km/h

⇒ Relative Speed in m/s = 110 × (5/18) = 275/9 m/s

⇒ Total Distance = Length of Train 1 + Length of Train 2 = 430 + L₂

⇒ 430 + L₂ = Relative Speed × Time

⇒ 430 + L₂ = (275/9) × 44

⇒ 430 + L₂ = 12100 / 9

⇒ 430 + L₂ = 1344.44 m

⇒ L₂ = 1344.44 − 430

⇒ L₂ = 914.44 m

**∴ The correct answer is 914.44 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed

When two bodies are moving in the same direction, relative speed = |S₁ − S₂|. When moving in opposite directions, relative speed = S₁ + S₂.

Crossing a Pole or Point Object

When a train crosses a stationary pole or a standing man, the distance covered is exactly equal to the length of the train itself.

Speed Conversion

To convert a value from km/h to m/s, multiply it by 5/18. To convert from m/s back to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

questions.question: Evaluate: 16 + 12 ÷ 4 - 3 × 3
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Expression to evaluate: 16 + 12 ÷ 4 - 3 × 3

**Formula Used:**

Follow the BODMAS rule: Brackets, Orders (i.e., powers and roots, etc.), Division and Multiplication (from left to right), Addition and Subtraction (from left to right).

**Calculation:**

Expression: 16 + 12 ÷ 4 - 3 × 3

⇒ 16 + 3 - 9

⇒ (16 + 3) - 9

⇒ 19 - 9

⇒ 10

**The value of the expression is 10.**

questions.question: X can complete a task in 15 days, and Y can complete the same task in 20 days. If X and Y work on alternate days starting with X, in how many days will the work be completed?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Work = LCM(15, 20) = 60 units.

Efficiency of X = 60 ÷ 15 = 4 units/day, Efficiency of Y = 60 ÷ 20 = 3 units/day.

Work done in a 2-day cycle (X + Y alternately) = 4 + 3 = 7 units.

In 8 full cycles (16 days), work done = 8 × 7 = 56 units.

Remaining work = 60 − 56 = 4 units, which X completes exactly in 1 day (on the 17th day).

**∴ The correct answer is 17 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 X
 15
 60
 60 ÷ 15 = 4
 
 

 Y
 20
 60 ÷ 20 = 3
 
 

⇒ Total work done in 1 cycle (2 days) = Efficiency of X + Efficiency of Y = 4 + 3 = 7 units.

⇒ Number of full cycles possible = 60 ÷ 7 = 8 cycles (with remainder).

⇒ Work completed in 8 cycles (8 × 2 = 16 days) = 8 × 7 = 56 units.

⇒ Remaining work = Total work − Work completed = 60 − 56 = 4 units.

⇒ On the 17th day, it is X's turn to work.

⇒ Time taken by X to complete the remaining 4 units = Remaining work ÷ Efficiency of X = 4 ÷ 4 = 1 day.

⇒ Total time taken = 16 days + 1 day = 17 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 17 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Alternate Day Working Concept

When individuals work on alternate days, calculate the combined work done in one complete cycle (usually 2 days for 2 people) and find the maximum full cycles before evaluating the remaining work turn by turn based on who started the work.

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the total amount of work physically done by each individual. If they work for the same number of days, the ratio of their wages will exactly equal the ratio of their daily efficiencies.

Pipes and Cisterns (Alternating)

Similar to alternate working in Time & Work, if one pipe fills and another empties alternately, the net work in one cycle is the difference in their efficiencies. Caution is always needed for the final cycle to ensure the tank is not over-calculated once filled.
</p

questions.question: Find the greatest number which on dividing 1657 and 2037, leaves remainders 6 and 5, respectively.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Required number = HCF of (1657 − 6) and (2037 − 5)

⇒ HCF of 1651 and 2032

Difference between the numbers = 2032 − 1651 = 381

The HCF must be a factor of their difference (381 = 3 × 127).

Since 1651 is not divisible by 3 (sum of digits is 13), the HCF is exactly 127.

**∴ The correct answer is 127.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Numbers = 1657 and 2037

Remainders = 6 and 5 respectively

**Formula Used:**

Greatest number = HCF of (First Number − First Remainder) and (Second Number − Second Remainder)

**Calculations:**

⇒ First number to be divided = 1657 − 6 = 1651

⇒ Second number to be divided = 2037 − 5 = 2032

⇒ We need to find the HCF of 1651 and 2032.

⇒ Prime factorization of 1651 = 13 × 127

⇒ Prime factorization of 2032 = 16 × 127 = 2⁴ × 127

⇒ The common factor in both factorizations is 127.

⇒ Therefore, the HCF of 1651 and 2032 is 127.

**∴ The correct answer is 127.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

HCF of Numbers Leaving Same Remainder

To find the greatest number that divides x, y, and z leaving the same remainder in each case, calculate the HCF of |x − y|, |y − z|, and |z − x|.

HCF of Numbers Leaving Different Remainders

To find the greatest number that divides x, y, and z leaving remainders a, b, and c respectively, calculate the HCF of (x − a), (y − b), and (z − c).

LCM of Numbers Leaving Same Remainder

The smallest number which when divided by x, y, and z leaves the same remainder r in each case is given by LCM(x, y, z) + r.

Relation between HCF and LCM

For any two numbers a and b, the product of the numbers is equal to the product of their HCF and LCM: a × b = HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b).
</p

questions.question: If 2% of x = 288, then x is equal to:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Given that 2% of a number x is 288.

To find the total value (100%), directly multiply both the percentage and the value by 50.

⇒ 2% × 50 = 100%

⇒ 288 × 50 = 14400

**∴ The correct answer is x = 14400.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

2% of x = 288

**Formula Used:**

Percentage Value = (Percentage ÷ 100) × Total Value

 
 
 
 2%
 Total x (100%)
 
 
• 
 

 288

 
• 
 

 x

 

 

 × 50

**Calculations:**

⇒ (2 ÷ 100) × x = 288

⇒ x = 288 × (100 ÷ 2)

⇒ x = 144 × 100

⇒ x = 14400

**∴ The correct answer is x = 14400.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage to Fraction Conversion

To convert a percentage into a fraction, divide it by 100 and simplify. Example: 2% = 2 ÷ 100 = 1/50.

Finding the Base Value

When a certain percentage of a quantity is given, the whole quantity (100%) can be directly found using the formula: Base = (Given Value ÷ Percentage) × 100.

Percentage Change

Percentage change = [(New Value − Original Value) ÷ Original Value] × 100. It measures the degree of growth or reduction of any given mathematical quantity.
</p

questions.question: The average weight of 27 students of a class is 53 kg. If the weight of the teacher is included, the average rises by 700 grams. Find the weight (in kg) of the teacher.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the Net Deviation Method for Averages:

Teacher's Weight = Old Average + (New Total People × Increase in Average)

Teacher's Weight = 53 + (28 × 0.7)

Teacher's Weight = 53 + 19.6 = 72.6 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 72.6 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 Teacher's Weight Breakup
 
 Old Average = 53 kg
 
 Total Increase
 (28 × 0.7 kg = 19.6 kg)
 

 Teacher's Weight = 53 + 19.6 = 72.6 kg

**Given:**

Number of students = 27

Average weight of 27 students = 53 kg

Average increase when teacher is included = 700 grams = 0.7 kg

**Formula Used:**

Total Weight = Average × Number of entities

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total weight of 27 students = 27 × 53 = 1431 kg

⇒ New number of people (students + teacher) = 28

⇒ New average weight = 53 + 0.7 = 53.7 kg

⇒ Total weight of 28 people = 28 × 53.7 = 1503.6 kg

⇒ Weight of the teacher = (Total weight of 28 people) − (Total weight of 27 students)

⇒ Weight of the teacher = 1503.6 − 1431 = 72.6 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 72.6 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Combined Average

When two groups of sizes n₁ and n₂ have averages A₁ and A₂, the combined average is (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Net Deviation Method

If a new value joins a group and changes the average, the new value = Old Average + (Total Number of people × Change in Average). A positive change means the new value is higher than the old average.

Replacement in Averages

When one person is replaced by another, the weight of the new person = Weight of the removed person + (Total Number of people × Change in Average).

questions.question: Mukund invests a sum of ₹5400 and Sachin invests a sum of ₹9400 at the same rate of simple interest per annum. If, at the end of 4 years, Sachin gets ₹960 more interest than Mukund, then find the rate of interest per annum (in percentage).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Difference in principal = ₹9400 − ₹5400 = ₹4000

This extra principal generates the extra interest of ₹960 over 4 years.

Rate (R) = (Difference in Interest × 100) ÷ (Difference in Principal × Time)

R = (960 × 100) ÷ (4000 × 4)

R = 96000 ÷ 16000 = 6

**∴ The correct answer is 6%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Mukund's Principal (P₁) = ₹5400

Sachin's Principal (P₂) = ₹9400

Time (T) = 4 years

Difference in Simple Interest = ₹960

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

questions.question: The cost price of a laptop is ₹78,200. If the loss percentage is 44%, then what is the selling price (in ₹) of the laptop?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Loss = 44% = 44 ÷ 100 = 11 ÷ 25

Cost Price (CP) = 25 units, Loss = 11 units

Selling Price (SP) = CP − Loss = 25 − 11 = 14 units

25 units = 78200 ⇒ 1 unit = 78200 ÷ 25 = 3128

Selling Price (14 units) = 14 × 3128 = 43792

**∴ The correct answer is ₹43,792.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost Price (CP) of the laptop = ₹78,200

Loss Percentage = 44%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = CP × [ (100 − Loss%) ÷ 100 ]

 
 Cost Price = 100% (₹78,200)

 
 SP = 56%

 
 Loss = 44%

 

 

 

 
 SP = 100% − 44% = 56% of CP

**Calculations:**

⇒ SP = 78200 × [ (100 − 44) ÷ 100 ]

⇒ SP = 78200 × (56 ÷ 100)

⇒ SP = 78200 × 0.56

⇒ SP = 782 × 56

⇒ SP = 43792

**∴ The correct answer is ₹43,792.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Basic Formulas

Profit = SP − CP | Loss = CP − SP.

Profit and Loss Percentage

Profit% = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100 | Loss% = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100. Always remember that both profit and loss percentages are calculated on the Cost Price by default.

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always offered on the Marked Price (MP). To find the selling price after a discount: SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100.

questions.question: The price of fuel decreases by 15%, 40% and 60% in three successive months, but increases by 45% in the fourth month. What is the percentage increase/decrease in the price of fuel in the fourth month as compared to its original price?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the initial price of fuel be 100.

Applying successive percentage multiplying factors:

Final Price = 100 × 0.85 × 0.60 × 0.40 × 1.45 = 29.58

Net percentage decrease = 100 − 29.58 = 70.42%

**∴ The correct answer is Decreases by 70.42%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Successive changes in fuel price: −15%, −40%, −60%, +45%

**Formula Used:**

Final Value = Initial Value × (1 ± R₁/100) × (1 ± R₂/100) × ...

 
 
 

 
 
 

 
 

 

 −15%

 

 −40%

 

 −60%

 

 +45%

 

 Net Decrease = 70.42%

 
 100
 Initial
 
 
 85
 
 
 51
 
 
 20.4
 
 
 29.58
 Final

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the original price of fuel be 100.

⇒ Price after 1st month (15% decrease) = 100 × (1 − 15/100) = 85

⇒ Price after 2nd month (40% decrease) = 85 × (1 − 40/100) = 85 × 0.60 = 51

⇒ Price after 3rd month (60% decrease) = 51 × (1 − 60/100) = 51 × 0.40 = 20.4

⇒ Price after 4th month (45% increase) = 20.4 × (1 + 45/100) = 20.4 × 1.45 = 29.58

⇒ Total decrease in price = Original Price − Final Price

⇒ Total decrease = 100 − 29.58 = 70.42

⇒ Percentage decrease = (70.42 ÷ 100) × 100 = 70.42%

**∴ The correct answer is Decreases by 70.42%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

If a value changes successively by a% and b%, the net percentage change can be calculated using the formula: Net Change = a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100. For a decrease, always use a negative sign.

Multiplying Factor Method

Instead of computing the percentage and subtracting, directly multiply the base by (1 ± R/100). For example, a 15% decrease uses a factor of 0.85, and a 45% increase uses 1.45. This method is exceptionally fast for successive changes.

Ratio Method for Successive Changes

Convert percentages to fractions. A 40% decrease (−2/5) leaves 3/5 of the value. The overall change ratio is simply the product of all individual fractional multipliers.
</p

questions.question: 400 pears were bought at ₹1230 per hundred and were sold at a profit of ₹980. Find the selling price (in ₹) per dozen of pears.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

SP for 100 pears = CP of 100 pears + Profit per 100 pears

SP for 100 pears = 1230 + (980 ÷ 4) = 1230 + 245 = ₹1475

SP for 1 pear = 1475 ÷ 100 = ₹14.75

SP for 1 dozen (12 pears) = 14.75 × 12 = ₹177

**∴ The correct answer is ₹177.**

questions.solution:

A ratio acts as a fraction where the first term is the numerator and the second is the denominator.

If Numerator > Denominator, the ratio's value is greater than 1.

If Numerator 13).

Therefore, 19 : 13 is strictly greater than 1, instantly making it the highest among all proper fraction options.

**∴ The correct answer is 19 : 13.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Four ratios: 15 : 19, 19 : 13, 12 : 19, and 21 : 26

**Concept Used:**

Convert each ratio to its decimal equivalent to compare their exact scale values.

 
• 
 
 15 : 19
 
 ≈ 0.79

 19 : 13
 
 ≈ 1.46 (Highest)

 12 : 19
 
 ≈ 0.63

 21 : 26
 
 ≈ 0.81

**Calculations:**

⇒ 15 : 19 = 15 ÷ 19 ≈ 0.789

⇒ 19 : 13 = 19 ÷ 13 ≈ 1.461

⇒ 12 : 19 = 12 ÷ 19 ≈ 0.631

⇒ 21 : 26 = 21 ÷ 26 ≈ 0.807

⇒ Comparing the decimal values: 1.461 > 0.807 > 0.789 > 0.631

⇒ The highest decimal value correctly corresponds to the ratio 19 : 13.

**∴ The correct answer is 19 : 13.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Proper vs Improper Fractions

A proper fraction has a numerator smaller than its denominator, ensuring its overall value is strictly less than 1. An improper fraction features a larger numerator, making its overall value directly greater than 1.

Cross-Multiplication Method

To effectively compare two fractions a/b and c/d without calculating decimals, cross-multiply. If (a × d) > (b × c), then it is proven that a/b > c/d.

Compound Ratio

The compound ratio of two individual ratios a : b and c : d is mathematically defined as ac : bd. It basically represents the direct multiplication of the two given fractions.

questions.question: If at same rate of interest, in 2 years, the simple interest is ₹44 and compound interest is ₹45, then what is the principal (in ₹)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For 2 years, Principal = (SI ÷ 2)² ÷ (CI − SI)

Given SI = ₹44 and CI = ₹45

Principal = (44 ÷ 2)² ÷ (45 − 44)

Principal = 22² ÷ 1 = 484

**∴ The correct answer is ₹484.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Simple interest (SI) for 2 years = ₹44

Compound interest (CI) for 2 years = ₹45

 
 Year 1: ₹22 (SI)
 
 Year 2: ₹22 (SI)
 

 

 
 CI Diff: ₹1 (on ₹22)
 Total SI = ₹44 | Total CI = ₹45
 Interest on 1st Year Interest

**Calculations:**

⇒ Simple interest for 1 year = 44 ÷ 2 = ₹22

⇒ Compound interest for 1st year = ₹22

⇒ Compound interest for 2nd year = Total CI − CI for 1st year

⇒ CI for 2nd year = 45 − 22 = ₹23

⇒ Difference in 2nd year interest = 23 − 22 = ₹1

⇒ This ₹1 is the interest earned on 1st year's interest (₹22) at rate R.

⇒ Rate (R) = (1 × 100) ÷ 22 = (50 ÷ 11)%

⇒ We know, SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

⇒ 22 = (P × (50 ÷ 11) × 1) ÷ 100

⇒ P = (22 × 100 × 11) ÷ 50

⇒ P = 22 × 2 × 11 = 484

**∴ The correct answer is ₹484.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Difference between CI and SI for 2 years:

D = P(R ÷ 100)², where P is the principal and R is the rate of interest.

Difference between CI and SI for 3 years:

D = P(R ÷ 100)²(3 + R ÷ 100).

SI vs CI:

Simple interest is calculated only on the principal amount, whereas compound interest is calculated on the principal and also on the accumulated interest of previous periods.

questions.question: The smallest natural number which is divisible by 24, 58, 48 and 12 is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The smallest number divisible by the given numbers is their LCM.

Notice that 48 is already a multiple of 12 and 24, so we can ignore 12 and 24.

We just need to find the LCM of 48 and 58.

Both 48 and 58 are divisible by 2: 48 = 24 × 2 and 58 = 29 × 2.

LCM(48, 58) = 24 × 29 × 2 = 48 × 29 = 1392.

**∴ The correct answer is 1392.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The numbers are 24, 58, 48, and 12.

**Concept Used:**

The smallest natural number exactly divisible by a given set of numbers is the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of those numbers.

**Calculations:**

Find the prime factorization of each number:

⇒ 12 = 2² × 3

⇒ 24 = 2³ × 3

⇒ 48 = 2⁴ × 3

⇒ 58 = 2¹ × 29

To find the LCM, take the highest power of each prime factor present:

⇒ LCM = 2⁴ × 3¹ × 29¹

⇒ LCM = 16 × 3 × 29

⇒ LCM = 48 × 29

⇒ LCM = 1392

**∴ The correct answer is 1392.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Least Common Multiple (LCM)

The LCM of two or more numbers is the smallest possible number that is a multiple of each of the given numbers.

Highest Common Factor (HCF)

The HCF of two or more numbers is the greatest number that divides each of them exactly without leaving any remainder.

LCM and HCF Relationship

For any two specific numbers a and b, the product of their LCM and HCF is equal to the product of the numbers themselves: LCM(a, b) × HCF(a, b) = a × b.

Co-prime Numbers

Two numbers are said to be co-prime if their HCF is 1. The LCM of any two co-prime numbers is simply their product.
</p

questions.question: Pravin has ₹1612 with him. He divided it amongst his sons Rishi and Shan and asked them to invest it at 8% rate of interest compounded annually. It was seen that Rishi and Shan got same amount after 17 and 18 years respectively. How much (in ₹) did Pravin give to Rishi?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When amounts are equal at CI, ratio of principal shares is P₁/P₂ = (1 + R/100)t² − t¹.

Difference in time for Rishi and Shan = 18 − 17 = 1 year.

Rishi's share ÷ Shan's share = (100 + 8) ÷ 100 = 108/100 = 27/25.

Total parts = 27 + 25 = 52 parts ≡ ₹1612 ⇒ 1 part = ₹31.

Rishi's share = 27 × 31 = ₹837.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹837.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total sum Pravin has = ₹1612

Rate of interest (R) = 8% compounded annually

Time for Rishi (t₁) = 17 years

Time for Shan (t₂) = 18 years

**Formula Used:**

A = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ

 
 
 

 
 

 
 
 Total = ₹1612
 
 
 
• 
 
• 
 
 
 
 Rishi (x)

 
 
 Shan (y)
 
 
 
• 
 
• 

 17 yrs @ 8%
 18 yrs @ 8%

 
 
 Equal Amount (A)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the amount given to Rishi be x and to Shan be y.

⇒ x + y = 1612

Since the amounts received by both are equal:

⇒ Amount of Rishi = Amount of Shan

⇒ x × (1 + 8/100)¹⁷ = y × (1 + 8/100)¹⁸

⇒ x / y = (1 + 8/100)¹⁸ − ¹⁷

⇒ x / y = (1 + 8/100)¹

⇒ x / y = 108 / 100

⇒ x / y = 27 / 25

⇒ Total ratio parts = 27 + 25 = 52 parts

⇒ 52 parts = 1612

⇒ 1 part = 1612 ÷ 52 = 31

⇒ Amount given to Rishi (x) = 27 parts

⇒ 27 × 31 = 837

**∴ The correct answer is ₹837.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest Formula

The amount after n years at compound interest is given by A = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ, where P is the principal and R is the rate.

Equal Amounts Distribution

If a total sum is split into P₁ and P₂ such that their amounts are equal after t₁ and t₂ years, then the ratio of their investments is P₁ / P₂ = (1 + R/100)t² − t¹.

Difference Between CI and SI

For the first year, CI and SI are exactly the same. For 2 years, the difference between CI and SI on a certain sum is given by D = P(R/100)².

questions.question: Find the average speed of Sanjay, who covers the first 150 km in 4 hours and the next 250 km in another 4 hours.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Average speed is the ratio of total distance travelled to total time taken.

Total Distance = 150 + 250 = 400 km

Total Time = 4 + 4 = 8 hours

Average Speed = 400 ÷ 8 = 50 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 50 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance 1 (D₁) = 150 km

Time 1 (T₁) = 4 hours

Distance 2 (D₂) = 250 km

Time 2 (T₂) = 4 hours

**Formula Used:**

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

 
• 
 
 
 
 
 150 km
 250 km
 
 4 hours
 4 hours
 
 

 Total Distance = 400 km, Total Time = 8 hours

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = D₁ + D₂ = 150 + 250 = 400 km

⇒ Total Time = T₁ + T₂ = 4 + 4 = 8 hours

⇒ Average Speed = 400 ÷ 8

⇒ Average Speed = 50 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 50 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed (Equal Distances)

When a person travels two equal distances at speeds x and y, Average Speed = (2xy) ÷ (x + y).

Average Speed (Equal Time)

When a person travels for two equal time periods at speeds x and y, Average Speed = (x + y) ÷ 2.

Speed Unit Conversion

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5 ÷ 18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18 ÷ 5.
</p
